questions.text:
Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

Less than a crore of rupees were sanctioned by him immediately.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Rupees was.
Key Points​

  • The use of 'Rupees were' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • Whenever adjectives such as much, less, little and more are used as nouns, they are always followed by a singular verb. Another Example:  – is the correct sentence.
  • Example:
    • Less than a litre of milk was consumed by them.
  • ​Hence, the underlined part of the sentence should be replaced by 'Rupees was'.
     

​Correct sentence: Less than a crore of rupees was sanctioned by him immediately. 

Additional Information

  • Let us see the meaning of the word 'Sanctioned':
    • Sanctioned: past tense of 'Sanction' which means to give official permission or approval for (an action).
    • Example:
      • The scheme was sanctioned by the court.

questions.text:
Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

Walk in the rain can be very enjoyable for kids.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Walking in the rain'.

Key Points​

  • The use of 'Walk in the rain' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • 'Walking in the rain' is a gerund phrase.
  • A whole gerund phrase functions in a sentence just like a noun, and can act as a subject, an object, or a predicate nominative.
  • Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by 'Walking in the rain'.
     

​Correct sentence: Walking in the rain can be very enjoyable for kids.

Additional Information

  • A "gerund phrase" is simply a noun phrase that starts with a gerund.
    • Example:
      • Getting a promotion is so exciting.

questions.text:
Given below is a sentence that may or may not be grammatically viable, choose the most suitable alternative that reflects the grammatically correct sentence.  

She spoke (less) Spanish so it was difficult to communicate with him. The language is very old and difficult to learn.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3)i.e. Little.

Key Points

  • The subject of the sentence is 'she' and here we are discussing her knowledge of 'spanish.'
  • The use of 'less' is incorrect.❌
  • The most appropriate determiner for the given sentence is ‘little'.
  • The determiner ‘little’ means ‘the value, the quantity about what is described in the sentence, is nearby zero’.   
  • We use little with uncountable nouns. Here, in the given sentence ‘Spanish’ is uncountable.
  • Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that option 3 is correct.✔️


📌Correct sentence: She spoke little Spanish so it was difficult to communicate with him. The language is very old and difficult to learn.✔️

Mistake Points 

  • We tend to go for option 4 but it would be wrong because ‘a little’ means ‘the amount described is small but there exists some amount in that.
  • Here, in the given question it has already been mentioned that the person faces a lot of difficulty in communicating in Spanish. Hence, it is almost impossible for that person to speak in Spanish.

Additional Information 

  • Let’s have a look at some rules:
  • A little, a few with the noun: We use a little with singular uncountable nouns. We use a few with plural countable nouns.
    • Example: It's a few inches beyond my reach.
    • Example: You're going a little fast.
  • Little, few with the noun: We use ‘little’ with uncountable nouns. We use ‘few’ with plural countable nouns. They are used in formal contexts and convey the quantity equivalent to nothing or negligible.
    • Example: He took what little money I had.

questions.text:
Given below is a sentence that may or may not be grammatically viable, choose the most suitable alternative that reflects the grammatically correct sentence. If the sentence does not require any correction, choose option 5. 'none of the above.'

Noah has lots doubts about the decisions. He believes that it is not possible for him to run as the mayor in the upcoming elections.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 1)i.e. some.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate determiner for the given sentence is ‘some.'
  • Because ‘some’ is generally used in a positive sentence or we can say in affirmative sentences.
  • We use the weak form of some only with uncountable nouns and plural nouns.
    • Example: Can you get some milk?
    • The quantity isn’t specified. Some suggest a normal amount, not an unlimited amount.
  • In the given sentence ‘doubts’ is a plural uncountable noun. and with it we should use 'some.'
  • Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that option 1 is correct.✔️

📌Correct sentence: Noah has some doubts about the decisions. He believes that it is not possible for him to run as the mayor in the upcoming elections.✔️

Additional Information 

  • We use ‘some’ with numbers. It can suggest an unexpectedly high amount.
    • Example: Some $50 billion was needed to rebuild the hospitals.

questions.text:
Direction: A sentence/a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, click the option corresponding to “No improvement”.

My grandmother told me a story as same as the hills.

options.text: A story as old as the hills
A story as well as the hills
A story as clear as the hills

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A story as old as the hills.
Key Points​

  • The use of the phrase 'A story as same as the hills' is inappropriate for the given sentence.
  • "As old as the hills" is an idiom which means very old.
  • Example:
    • The technology we're using is as old as the hills.
  • ​ 'A story as old as the hills' is a noun phrase.
  • ​Hence, the underlined phrase should be replaced by the phrase 'A story as old as the hills'.
     

​Correct sentence: My grandmother told me a story as old as the hills.

Additional Information

  • Let us see the meaning of 'Noun phrase':
    • 'Noun phrases' are groups of words that function as a noun.
    • Typically, they act as subjects, objects, or prepositional objects in a sentence. 
    • Example:
      • The spotted puppy is up for adoption.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

As an actor, Rohan is superior than any other twentieth-century actor.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'to'.

Key Points

  • Here in the given sentence, 'superior than' is used which is wrong.
  • Adjectives that end in 'ior' are followed by 'to' and not 'than'.
    • Example: He is junior to me.
  • In the given sentence 'superior than' is used, it should be replaced by 'superior to'.
  • 'Superior then' is wrong because then means next.

The correct sentence: As an actor, Rohan is superior to any other twentieth-century actor.

questions.text:
Given below is a sentence that may or may not be grammatically viable, choose the most suitable alternative that reflects the grammatically correct sentence. 

The judge would often rule the exact opposite of what the Chief justice had meant on a previous occasion, then both would be right. As both, their arguments would be right.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3)i.e. yet. 

Key Points

  • In the given sentence there are two subjects 'the judge' and the 'Chief justice' and the contradiction is that the judge has ruled against the chief justice's previous decision.
  • Let us explore the given option.
  • The conjunction ‘and’ is used to connect words of the same part of speech, clauses or sentences that are to be taken jointly. 
    • Example: James and Sam went to town.
    • Both individuals have gone to town and are joined by 'and'.
  • Here we are talking about two contrasting ideas. So option 1 is incorrect.❌
  • The conjunction ‘so’ means and for this reason; therefore. 
    • Example: He slept late so that he could finish the movie.
    • Here the explanation or reason for sleeping late has been explained by using 'so.'
  • There is no justification being given in the further parts of the given sentence.
  • So option 2 is incorrect. ❌
  • The conjunction ‘yet’ means but at the same time, but nevertheless. .
    • Example: He was smart yet he panicked and lost the fight.
    • 'yet' expresses the fact that even though he was 'smart' he still lost the fight as he 'panicked.'
  • Here in the latter parts, we are trying to show contrast that even though the ruling was different yet both sides still agree with each other
  • So option 3 is correct. ✔️
  • The conjunction ‘nor’ is used before the second or further of two or more alternatives to indicate that they are each untrue or each does not happen. Here we are talking about two events that have occurred and are true. So option 4 is incorrect.❌
  • The conjunction ‘or’ is used to link alternatives. Here we do not have to choose from two options,
    • Example: Orange or mango pick one.
    • We have to choose between an orange or mango.
  • So option 5, is incorrect.❌

📌Correct sentence: The judge would often rule the exact opposite of what the Chief justice had meant on a previous occasion, yet both would be right. As both, their arguments would be right.✔️

Additional Information

  • Another is singular. We don’t use it with plural nouns.
    • Example: Another interesting places to visit include the old harbor and the castle.❌(Incorrect)
    • Example: Other interesting places to visit include the old harbor and the castle.✔️(Correct)
  • We write another as one word.
    • Example: There is an other car park a little further down the same street.❌ (Incorrect)
    • Example: There is another car park a little further down the same street.✔️(Correct)
  • The words another and other mean the same thing, except that another is used with a singular noun and the other is used with uncountable and plural nouns.

questions.text:
In the following sentence, a part of the sentence is underlined. Below are given alternatives to the underlined part, which may improve the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed, choose the alternative that indicates 'No improvement'.

Because anyone with halves of the eyes could have easily detected the fraud, it's highly likely that the swindling diamond merchant had inside help.

options.text: anyone with half of the eyes
anyone with halving of an eye

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option (3) i.e. anyone with half an eye

Key Points

  • The correct idiomatic expression is 'half an eye' and not ‘halves of the eyes'.
  • Half an eye (Idiom): Intermittent or half-hearted attention.
    • E.g. Anyone with half an eye could see Susan's antagonism towards her.
  • Hence ‘half an eye’ should be used in place of ‘halves of the eyes’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • Among the given choices, only option 3 replaces the given underlined part most appropriately.
  • Hence, Option 3 is the correct answer.
     
Correct sentence: ​Because anyone with half an eye could have easily detected the fraud, it's highly likely that the swindling diamond merchant had inside help.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement".

Subhash Chandra Bose was a real-life hero, isn't he?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'wasn't he?'.

Key Points

  • Here in the given sentence, the wrong question tag has been used.
  • If the sentence is positive, the question tag must be negative and vice versa.
  • Always use pronoun in the question tag.
  • For the negative question tag, use the contracted form of 'helping verb' and 'not'.
    • Example: didn't, won't, etc.
  • Here the given sentence is positive, so here negative question tag will be used.
  • In the given sentence, 'isn't' will be replaced by 'wasn't' because the sentence is in the past tense.

The correct sentence: Subhash Chandra Bose was a real-life hero, wasn't he?

Additional Information 

  •  What is a question tag?
    • ​A question tag is a confirmatory question asked from the second person.

questions.text:
A sentence/ a part of the sentence is underlined. Five alternatives are given to the underlined part which will improve the meaning of the sentence. Choose the correct alternative. In case no improvement is needed. Click the option corresponding to "No improvement."

Raman is smarter than intelligent.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'more smart'.

Key Points

  • Here in the given sentence, 'smarter' is used which is wrong.
  • When two qualities of a noun or a pronoun are compared with each other, more+ positive degree is used instead of a comparative degree.
  • Here two qualities of Raman are compared with each other so, 'smarter' will be replaced by 'more smart'.

The correct sentence is Raman is more smart than intelligent.
